meta.description: This program allows bank staff to update credit card details (cardholder name, expiry date, and active status) for an existing credit card through a validated, confirmation-based online screen workflow.
meta.process_description: Bank staff first retrieve a specific credit card record by entering an account number and card number; the program displays the current card details on screen for review. Staff can then modify editable fields — the embossed cardholder name, card expiry month/year, and card active status (Y/N) — after which the program validates all changes before presenting them for confirmation. Upon confirmation (F5), the program locks the card record, checks it has not been changed by another user in the interim, and commits the update to the card database; if locking or saving fails, an appropriate error is shown and the update is rolled back.

files.CARDDAT: Primary credit card data file storing card records (card number, account ID, CVV, embossed name, expiry date, active status)
files.CARDAIX: Alternate index path on the card data file allowing lookup of card records by account ID rather than card number

business_rules: Account number is mandatory, must be numeric, exactly 11 digits, and non-zero before a card record can be retrieved
Card number is mandatory, must be numeric and exactly 16 digits
Embossed cardholder name is mandatory and may only contain alphabetic characters and spaces (no numbers or special characters)
Card active status must be either 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive); no other values are permitted
Card expiry month must be a valid calendar month between 1 and 12
Card expiry year must fall within the range 1950 to 2099
A two-step confirmation workflow is enforced: changes are validated first, then staff must explicitly confirm (F5) before the database is updated

Before committing an update, the program compares the current database record against the originally retrieved snapshot to detect concurrent modification by another user; if the record has changed, the update is rejected and staff are asked to re-review
The card record must be successfully locked before any update is applied; failure to lock prevents the update from proceeding
If no changes are detected between the original retrieved values and the values submitted by staff, the update is not processed and staff are informed
The program supports navigation back to the card list screen (COCRDSLC) or the main menu, allowing staff to exit without saving

variables.name: WS-MISC-STORAGE
variables.description: Top-level working storage container grouping all miscellaneous variables used during the card update process, including CICS processing variables, validation flags, and screen editing fields.

variables.name: WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to manage the technical communication with the CICS transaction processing environment during the card update workflow.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each file or system operation (e.g., reading or writing the card record). Used to determine whether the operation succeeded or failed, driving error handling such as detecting a locked record or a failed database write.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code providing additional detail about why a file or system operation failed. Used alongside the response code to diagnose specific error conditions, such as why a card record could not be locked for update.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier associated with the current card update session. Used to identify which transaction is running so the program can manage screen flow and return correctly to the appropriate point in the workflow.

variables.name: WS-UCTRANS
variables.description: An uppercase version of the transaction identifier, used to ensure consistent comparison and routing logic regardless of how the transaction ID was entered or passed by the calling program.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-FLAG
variables.description: Overall input validation status flag for the card update screen. Tracks whether the data entered by bank staff has passed all validation checks, failed validation, or is still awaiting initial input before any validation has been attempted.

variables.name: INPUT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that all fields entered by bank staff on the card update screen have passed validation and the update workflow may proceed to the confirmation step.

variables.name: INPUT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that one or more fields entered by bank staff on the card update screen have failed validation. The screen will be redisplayed with error messages so the staff member can correct the invalid data.

variables.name: INPUT-PENDING
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card update screen has been displayed but the bank staff member has not yet submitted any input for validation. Represents the initial state before the first submission.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ACCT-FLAG
variables.description: Validation flag for the account number entered on the card update screen. Records whether the account number is valid (numeric, exactly 11 digits, non-zero), invalid, or has not yet been entered, controlling whether the card record can be retrieved.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the account number entered by bank staff has failed validation — it may be non-numeric, not exactly 11 digits, or zero — and the card record cannot be retrieved until a valid account number is provided.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the account number entered by bank staff has passed all validation rules (numeric, exactly 11 digits, non-zero) and is acceptable for use in retrieving the associated card record.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the account number field has been left blank by bank staff. The account number is mandatory, so this condition triggers a prompt requiring the staff member to enter a value before proceeding.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CARD-FLAG
variables.description: Validation flag for the credit card number entered on the card update screen. Records whether the card number is valid (numeric, exactly 16 digits), invalid, or has not yet been entered, controlling whether the card record can be retrieved and updated.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the credit card number entered by bank staff has failed validation — it may be non-numeric or not exactly 16 digits — and the card record cannot be retrieved or updated until a valid card number is provided.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the credit card number entered by bank staff has passed all validation rules (numeric, exactly 16 digits) and is acceptable for use in retrieving and updating the card record.

variables.name: FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the credit card number field has been left blank by bank staff. The card number is mandatory, so this condition triggers a prompt requiring the staff member to enter a value before proceeding.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CARDNAME-FLAG
variables.description: Validation flag for the embossed cardholder name entered on the card update screen. Records whether the name contains only alphabetic characters and spaces (valid), contains invalid characters such as numbers or special characters (invalid), or has not yet been entered.

variables.name: FLG-CARDNAME-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the embossed cardholder name entered by bank staff has failed validation because it contains characters other than letters and spaces (e.g., digits or special characters). The name must be corrected before the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-CARDNAME-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the embossed cardholder name entered by bank staff contains only alphabetic characters and spaces, satisfying the business rule for what may appear on a physical credit card.

variables.name: FLG-CARDNAME-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the embossed cardholder name field has been left blank by bank staff. Since the cardholder name is mandatory on a credit card, this condition triggers a prompt requiring the staff member to enter a value.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CARDSTATUS-FLAG
variables.description: Validation flag for the card active status entered on the card update screen. Records whether the status value is acceptable (Y for active or N for inactive), unacceptable (any other value), or has not yet been entered. This controls whether the card can be activated or deactivated.

variables.name: FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the card active status entered by bank staff is neither 'Y' (active) nor 'N' (inactive), violating the business rule that only these two values are permitted. The status must be corrected before the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-CARDSTATUS-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the card active status entered by bank staff is either 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive), satisfying the business rule and allowing the update workflow to continue.

variables.name: FLG-CARDSTATUS-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the card active status field has been left blank by bank staff. Since the active status is required to determine whether the card is usable, this condition triggers a prompt requiring the staff member to enter a value.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CARDEXPMON-FLAG
variables.description: Validation flag for the card expiry month entered on the card update screen. Records whether the month is a valid calendar month (1 through 12), invalid, or has not yet been entered. This ensures the card expiry date is a real, usable date.

variables.name: FLG-CARDEXPMON-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the card expiry month entered by bank staff is outside the valid range of 1 to 12, meaning it does not correspond to a real calendar month. The month must be corrected before the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-CARDEXPMON-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the card expiry month entered by bank staff is a valid calendar month between 1 and 12, satisfying the business rule and allowing the update workflow to continue.

variables.name: FLG-CARDEXPMON-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the card expiry month field has been left blank by bank staff. Since the expiry month is required to form a valid card expiry date, this condition triggers a prompt requiring the staff member to enter a value.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CARDEXPYEAR-FLAG
variables.description: Validation flag for the card expiry year entered on the card update screen. Records whether the year falls within the accepted business range (1950 to 2099), is outside that range, or has not yet been entered. This ensures the card expiry date is within a meaningful and supported timeframe.

variables.name: FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating the card expiry year entered by bank staff falls outside the accepted range of 1950 to 2099, making it an implausible or unsupported expiry year. The year must be corrected before the update can proceed.

variables.name: FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the card expiry year entered by bank staff falls within the accepted range of 1950 to 2099, satisfying the business rule and allowing the update workflow to continue.

variables.name: FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating the card expiry year field has been left blank by bank staff. Since the expiry year is required to form a valid card expiry date, this condition triggers a prompt requiring the staff member to enter a value.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG
variables.description: Flag controlling whether the card update program should return control to the calling program (such as the card list screen or main menu) after completing its current processing cycle. Used to manage navigation flow when bank staff choose to exit the update screen.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating the card update program should continue its own processing and not yet return control to the calling program. The bank staff member is still actively working within the card update workflow.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating the card update program should return control to the calling program (e.g., the card list screen or main menu), typically because the bank staff member has chosen to exit the update workflow without saving changes.

variables.name: WS-PFK-FLAG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the function key pressed by bank staff is a recognised and supported key for the card update screen. Used to prevent the program from acting on unsupported keystrokes and to display an appropriate error message when an invalid key is pressed.

variables.name: PFK-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the function key pressed by bank staff is a recognised key for the card update screen (e.g., Enter, F3 to exit, F5 to confirm), and the program can proceed with the corresponding action.

variables.name: PFK-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating the function key pressed by bank staff is not supported on the card update screen. The program will display an error message informing the staff member to use a valid key.

variables.name: CARD-NAME-CHECK
variables.description: Temporary working area used to hold the embossed cardholder name during character-by-character validation, checking that every character is either a letter or a space before the name is accepted for update on the card record.

variables.name: FLG-YES-NO-CHECK
variables.description: Temporary working area used to hold the card active status value during validation, checking that it is either 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive) before it is accepted as a valid status change.

variables.name: FLG-YES-NO-VALID
variables.description: Condition confirming that the card active status value is one of the two permitted values: 'Y' meaning the card is active and available for use, or 'N' meaning the card is inactive and should be declined at point of sale.

variables.name: CARD-MONTH-CHECK
variables.description: Temporary working area holding the card expiry month as entered by bank staff in character format, used as the source for numeric conversion and range validation before the month is accepted as part of the card expiry date.

variables.name: CARD-MONTH-CHECK-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the card expiry month field, allowing the character input to be treated as a number for range validation. Enables the program to check whether the entered month falls between 1 and 12 without requiring a separate numeric field.

variables.name: VALID-MONTH
variables.description: Condition confirming that the card expiry month entered by bank staff corresponds to a real calendar month, falling between January (1) and December (12). Months outside this range are rejected as invalid expiry dates.

variables.name: CARD-YEAR-CHECK
variables.description: Temporary working area holding the card expiry year as entered by bank staff in character format, used as the source for numeric conversion and range validation before the year is accepted as part of the card expiry date.

variables.name: CARD-YEAR-CHECK-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the card expiry year field, allowing the character input to be treated as a number for range validation. Enables the program to check whether the entered year falls within the accepted business range of 1950 to 2099.

variables.name: VALID-YEAR
variables.description: Condition confirming that the card expiry year entered by bank staff falls within the range of years the system supports for credit card expiry dates (1950 to 2099). Years outside this range are rejected as implausible or unsupported.

variables.name: CICS-OUTPUT-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: Group of working variables used to hold card data fields in both character and numeric formats during screen input processing and output formatting, bridging between what bank staff enter on screen and the validated values written to the card record.

variables.name: CARD-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: The account number associated with the credit card, held in character format as entered by bank staff on the update screen. Used as the starting point for validation before being converted to numeric form for database lookup.

variables.name: CARD-ACCT-ID-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the account number field, allowing the character input to be validated as a proper numeric value and used for database retrieval via the card data file or alternate index.

variables.name: CARD-CVV-CD-X
variables.description: The card verification value (CVV) security code of the credit card, held in character format. Although not directly editable by bank staff in this update workflow, it is carried as part of the card record to ensure the full record is preserved when writing updates back to the database.

variables.name: CARD-CVV-CD-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the CVV security code field, used when the CVV needs to be processed or compared as a numeric value rather than a character string.

variables.name: CARD-CARD-NUM-X
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number as entered by bank staff on the update screen, held in character format. Used as the primary key for locating the card record in the card data file and must be validated as numeric and exactly 16 digits before the record can be retrieved.

variables.name: CARD-CARD-NUM-N
variables.description: Numeric reinterpretation of the credit card number field, allowing the character input to be validated as a proper numeric value and used as the key for direct lookup in the card data file (CARDDAT).

variables.name: CARD-NAME-EMBOSSED-X
variables.description: The cardholder name as it will appear physically embossed on the credit card, entered by bank staff on the update screen. This is one of the three editable fields in the card update workflow and must contain only alphabetic characters and spaces.

variables.name: CARD-STATUS-X
variables.description: The active status of the credit card as entered by bank staff on the update screen, indicating whether the card is currently active ('Y') or inactive ('N'). This is one of the three editable fields in the card update workflow and directly controls whether the card can be used for transactions.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-X
variables.description: The card expiry date as a formatted character string (e.g., MM/YYYY or similar), representing the date after which the credit card is no longer valid. This is one of the three editable fields in the card update workflow and is broken down into separate month and year components for individual validation.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A structured reinterpretation of the card expiry date character string, breaking it into its component parts (month and year) so that each element can be individually extracted, validated against business rules, and stored separately in the card record.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR
variables.description: The four-digit year portion of the credit card's expiry date (e.g., 2026). Used during validation to ensure the card has not expired and that the year falls within the accepted business range of 1950–2099 before the record is saved.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character (typically a slash or dash) between the year and month portions of the expiry date as stored or displayed on screen. Has no business meaning of its own but ensures the date is formatted correctly for readability.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-MONTH
variables.description: The two-digit month portion of the credit card's expiry date (01–12). Used during validation to confirm the card expiry month is a valid calendar month before the updated card record is committed to the database.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A separator character between the month and day portions of the expiry date. Has no business meaning of its own but maintains the expected date format in the stored or displayed card record.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-DAY
variables.description: The two-digit day portion of the credit card's expiry date. While credit cards typically expire at month-end, this field stores the day component of the expiry date as held in the card record on the CARDDAT file.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-N
variables.description: A numeric reinterpretation of the card expiry date field, allowing the program to perform numeric comparisons or arithmetic on the expiry date (e.g., range checks). This alternate view of the same storage supports validation logic without requiring separate data movement.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID
variables.description: The record identifier (RID) structure used to locate a specific credit card record in the CARDDAT file. Contains both the card number and account ID, giving the program the keys it needs to read, lock, and update the correct card record.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number used as the primary key to locate the card record in the CARDDAT file. This is the unique identifier for the physical card being updated by bank staff.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The 11-digit account ID associated with the credit card, stored in numeric format. Used as the alternate index key when looking up card records via the CARDAIX path, allowing staff to find a card by account number rather than card number.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: An alphanumeric reinterpretation of the account ID field, allowing the program to treat the account number as character data when needed (e.g., for screen display, string comparison, or passing to CICS commands that require character keys).

variables.name: WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE
variables.description: A structured diagnostic message assembled when a file operation (read, write, update) fails. Captures the operation name, file name, and CICS response codes so that bank staff or support teams can understand what went wrong during a card record access attempt.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed label text at the start of the file error message (e.g., 'FILE ERROR: '). Provides human-readable context so the error message is understandable when displayed to staff or written to a log.

variables.name: ERROR-OPNAME
variables.description: The name of the file operation that failed (e.g., 'READ', 'WRITE', 'REWRITE'). Tells support staff exactly which action was being attempted on the card file when the error occurred, aiding in diagnosis and resolution.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing or connector text between the operation name and file name in the error message (e.g., ' ON '). Improves readability of the error message displayed to bank staff or logged for support.

variables.name: ERROR-FILE
variables.description: The name of the file that experienced the error (e.g., 'CARDDAT' or 'CARDAIX'). Identifies which data store was involved in the failure, helping support staff pinpoint whether the issue is with the primary card file or the alternate index.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing or label text between the file name and the CICS response code in the error message (e.g., ' RESP: '). Maintains the readability and structure of the diagnostic error message.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP
variables.description: The primary CICS response code returned when the file operation failed. This numeric code indicates the category of error (e.g., record not found, file unavailable) and is essential for technical support to diagnose the root cause of a card file access failure.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing or label text between the primary and secondary CICS response codes in the error message (e.g., ' RESP2:'). Maintains the structure and readability of the diagnostic message.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP2
variables.description: The secondary CICS response code (RESP2) returned when the file operation failed. Provides additional detail beyond the primary response code, helping technical support pinpoint the exact nature of the card file error (e.g., specific lock conflict or I/O condition).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing padding at the end of the file error message structure. Ensures the message field is fully padded to its defined length for consistent display or logging.

variables.name: WS-LONG-MSG
variables.description: A large free-form message area used to hold extended diagnostic or informational text during processing. May be used to capture detailed error descriptions or debug information that exceeds the length of the standard short message fields, supporting troubleshooting of card update failures.

variables.name: WS-INFO-MSG
variables.description: The short informational message displayed to bank staff on the card update screen, guiding them through the update workflow. Its value is controlled by the 88-level condition names below, each representing a specific stage or outcome in the card update process.

variables.name: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that no informational message needs to be shown to bank staff at this point in the workflow. The screen info message area is blank or cleared.

variables.name: FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT
variables.description: Condition indicating that card records were successfully found for the account number entered by bank staff. Signals that the program can proceed to display the card details for review and editing.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting bank staff to enter the account number and/or card number to search for the card record they wish to update. This is the initial data-entry stage of the workflow.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card record has been retrieved and displayed, and the screen is now prompting bank staff to enter the changes they wish to make (e.g., new cardholder name, expiry date, or active status).

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION
variables.description: Condition indicating that the entered changes have passed all validation checks and the screen is now prompting bank staff to press F5 to confirm and permanently save the updated card details. This enforces the two-step confirmation workflow.

variables.name: CONFIRM-UPDATE-SUCCESS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card update has been successfully confirmed and committed to the CARDDAT file. The screen displays a success message to bank staff confirming the card details have been saved.

variables.name: INFORM-FAILURE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card update process has failed (e.g., due to a file error, lock failure, or concurrent modification). The screen informs bank staff that the update could not be completed and they may need to retry or escalate.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG
variables.description: The primary message displayed to bank staff on the card update screen, communicating the result of their last action or guiding them to the next required step. Its content is determined by the 88-level conditions below, covering all key business outcomes and validation errors in the card update workflow.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that no return message is currently set. The message area on the card update screen is blank, typically at the start of a new interaction before any action has been taken.

variables.name: WS-EXIT-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that a message is being shown to bank staff as they exit the card update screen, typically confirming they are navigating away without saving changes.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting bank staff to enter a valid account number. Displayed when the account number field is missing or has not yet been provided.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-CARD
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting bank staff to enter a valid card number. Displayed when the card number field is missing or has not yet been provided.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-NAME
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting bank staff to enter the embossed cardholder name. Displayed when the name field is blank and must be populated before the update can proceed.

variables.name: WS-NAME-MUST-BE-ALPHA
variables.description: Condition indicating a validation error: the cardholder name entered by bank staff contains non-alphabetic characters (e.g., numbers or special characters). The business rule requires the embossed name to contain only letters and spaces.

variables.name: NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED
variables.description: Condition indicating that bank staff submitted the search form without entering any account number or card number. The program cannot retrieve a card record without at least one search key.

variables.name: NO-CHANGES-DETECTED
variables.description: Condition indicating that bank staff submitted the update form but the values entered are identical to the original card data already on file. The program will not process a redundant update and informs staff that no changes were detected.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-ZEROES
variables.description: Condition indicating a validation error: the account number entered by bank staff is all zeros, which is not a valid account identifier. The business rule requires the account number to be non-zero.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-NOT-NUMERIC
variables.description: Condition indicating a validation error: the account number entered by bank staff contains non-numeric characters. The business rule requires the account number to be exactly 11 numeric digits.

variables.name: SEARCHED-CARD-NOT-NUMERIC
variables.description: Condition indicating a validation error: the card number entered by bank staff contains non-numeric characters. The business rule requires the card number to be exactly 16 numeric digits.

variables.name: CARD-STATUS-MUST-BE-YES-NO
variables.description: Condition indicating a validation error: the card active status entered by bank staff is not 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive). Only these two values are permitted by the business rules for card status.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-MONTH-NOT-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating a validation error: the expiry month entered by bank staff is not a valid calendar month (must be between 01 and 12). The card record cannot be updated with an invalid expiry month.

variables.name: CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR-NOT-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating a validation error: the expiry year entered by bank staff falls outside the accepted range of 1950 to 2099. The card record cannot be updated with an out-of-range expiry year.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by bank staff could not be found in the card cross-reference (CARDAIX alternate index). No card records are associated with this account in the system.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCTCARD-COMBO
variables.description: Condition indicating that the specific combination of account number and card number entered by bank staff does not exist in the CARDDAT file. The card number may not belong to the specified account.

variables.name: COULD-NOT-LOCK-FOR-UPDATE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the program was unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the card record before applying the update. This prevents the update from proceeding to avoid data corruption, and bank staff are informed to try again later.

variables.name: DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE
variables.description: Condition indicating that another user modified the card record between the time bank staff retrieved it and the time they attempted to save their changes. The update is rejected to prevent overwriting the other user's changes, and staff are asked to re-review the current data.

variables.name: LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card record was successfully locked for update, but the actual write operation to the CARDDAT file subsequently failed. This is an unexpected system error requiring investigation, as the lock was obtained but the data could not be saved.

variables.name: XREF-READ-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that an error occurred while reading the CARDAIX alternate index file during the card lookup process. This is a system-level file access failure that prevents the card record from being retrieved by account ID.

variables.name: CODING-TO-BE-DONE
variables.description: Condition used as a development placeholder, indicating that a particular code path or business scenario has not yet been fully implemented. Should not appear in a production environment and signals incomplete functionality to developers.

variables.name: WS-LITERALS
variables.description: A group of constant reference values (literals) that identify the key programs, transaction IDs, map sets, and maps involved in the card update workflow. These values are used for CICS navigation and screen control, ensuring the program correctly routes staff between screens.

variables.name: LIT-THISPGM
variables.description: The name of the current program (COCRDUPC), the card update program itself. Used in CICS commands and communication areas to identify this program as the source of a transaction or return address.

variables.name: LIT-THISTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID associated with the card update program. Used to initiate or re-enter this transaction, ensuring the correct program is invoked when bank staff are working on a card update.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAPSET
variables.description: The name of the BMS map set used by the card update program (COCRDUP). Identifies the collection of screen maps that define the layout of the card update screen displayed to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAP
variables.description: The name of the specific BMS map within the map set that defines the card update screen layout. Used in CICS SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP commands to display and receive the card update form.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTPGM
variables.description: The name of the card list program (COCRDSLC) that bank staff can navigate back to from the card update screen. Used when staff press the back/cancel key to return to the card selection list without saving changes.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the card list program. Used to transfer control back to the card list screen when bank staff choose to exit the card update screen and return to the list of cards for an account.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS map set name for the card list screen. Used when navigating back to the card list program to ensure the correct screen layout is displayed to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name within the card list map set. Used when returning to the card list screen to ensure the correct map is sent to the bank staff member's terminal.

variables.name: LIT-MENUPGM
variables.description: The fixed program name of the main menu application. Used when staff navigate back to the CardDemo main menu, telling CICS which program to transfer control to.

variables.name: LIT-MENUTRANID
variables.description: The fixed CICS transaction ID associated with the main menu screen. Used to initiate the main menu transaction when a staff member chooses to exit the card update workflow and return to the menu.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAPSET
variables.description: The fixed BMS mapset name for the main menu screen. Used to load the correct set of screen definitions when displaying the main menu to staff.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAP
variables.description: The fixed BMS map name for the main menu screen. Identifies the specific screen layout to display when staff are redirected to the main menu.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLPGM
variables.description: The fixed program name of the card list/detail screen (COCRDSLC). Used when staff choose to navigate back to the card selection list rather than completing the update.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLTRANID
variables.description: The fixed CICS transaction ID for the card list/detail screen. Used to initiate the card list transaction when staff navigate away from the card update screen.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAPSET
variables.description: The fixed BMS mapset name for the card list/detail screen. Used to load the correct screen definitions when returning staff to the card selection list.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAP
variables.description: The fixed BMS map name for the card list/detail screen. Identifies the specific screen layout to display when staff are redirected back to the card selection list.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME
variables.description: The fixed CICS file name for the primary credit card data file (CARDDAT). Used when reading or updating a card record directly by card number as the primary key.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH
variables.description: The fixed CICS file name for the alternate index path on the card file (CARDAIX). Used when looking up a card record by account ID rather than card number, allowing staff to find a card when they know the account but not the card number.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM
variables.description: A reference string containing all alphabetic characters (both upper and lower case) and spaces, used as the source set in an INSPECT or translation operation to validate that the embossed cardholder name contains only permitted characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A reference string of spaces, used as the target/replacement set when validating the embossed cardholder name. Any character in the name that matches an allowed character is effectively 'cancelled out', leaving only invalid characters detectable.

variables.name: LIT-UPPER
variables.description: A reference string containing all 26 uppercase alphabetic characters (A–Z). Used in character translation or validation routines to convert or check the embossed cardholder name for uppercase letters.

variables.name: LIT-LOWER
variables.description: A reference string containing all 26 lowercase alphabetic characters (a–z). Used alongside LIT-UPPER in character translation routines to handle or convert lowercase letters in the embossed cardholder name.

variables.name: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
variables.description: The working storage communication area specific to this card update program. Holds all state information that must be preserved between screen interactions during the card update workflow, including the workflow stage, original card data snapshot, and the new data entered by staff.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-SCREEN-DATA
variables.description: Groups the workflow control data for the card update screen, tracking where in the update process the staff member currently is.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION
variables.description: A single-character workflow state flag that tracks which stage of the card update process the staff member is currently in. Controls the program's behaviour at each step: whether to fetch card details, display them, validate changes, await confirmation, commit the update, or handle a failure.

variables.name: CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED
variables.description: Condition indicating that no card record has been retrieved yet. The staff member has not yet provided a valid account/card number to look up, so the update workflow has not started.

variables.name: CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card record has been successfully retrieved and its current details are being displayed to the staff member for review before any changes are made.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGES-MADE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the staff member has submitted changes to the card details. Covers both the case where the changes failed validation and the case where they passed validation and are awaiting confirmation.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the changes submitted by the staff member failed one or more business validation rules (e.g. invalid expiry month, non-alphabetic name). The staff member must correct the errors before proceeding.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the submitted changes have passed all validation checks but the staff member has not yet pressed F5 to confirm. The program is waiting for explicit confirmation before writing to the database.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the staff member confirmed the changes (pressed F5), the update was successfully written to the card database, and the workflow is complete.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGES-FAILED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the confirmed update could not be saved to the database, either because the record could not be locked or because the save operation itself failed. Staff must be informed and may need to retry.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that the card record could not be exclusively locked for update, meaning another process may be using it. The update is blocked to prevent data corruption, and staff are informed they cannot save at this time.

variables.name: CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the update was confirmed and the record was locked, but the actual write to the card database failed (e.g. due to a concurrent modification by another user or a system error). Staff must be informed of the failure.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-DETAILS
variables.description: A snapshot of the card record as it existed when first retrieved from the database. Preserved throughout the update workflow so that, at the moment of saving, the program can detect whether another user has modified the record in the meantime, protecting data integrity.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-ACCTID
variables.description: The account ID as originally retrieved from the database. Retained in the snapshot to confirm the card still belongs to the same account when the update is committed.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-CARDID
variables.description: The 16-digit card number as originally retrieved from the database. Used as the key to re-read and lock the card record at confirmation time, and to detect if the record has been replaced.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-CVV-CD
variables.description: The card's CVV security code as originally retrieved. Included in the snapshot to detect any concurrent modification to the record; CVV is not editable by staff in this screen.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA
variables.description: Groups the editable card data fields as they existed at the time of retrieval. This group is compared against the current database record before saving to detect concurrent changes by another user.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME
variables.description: The cardholder's embossed name as it appeared on the card record when originally retrieved. Used to detect if another user has changed the name between retrieval and the attempted save.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-EXPIRAION-DATE
variables.description: The card's expiry date as originally retrieved from the database, broken into year, month, and day components. Used in the concurrent modification check before committing the update.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR
variables.description: The four-digit expiry year of the card as originally retrieved (e.g. 2026). Part of the original snapshot used to detect concurrent changes before saving.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-EXPMON
variables.description: The two-digit expiry month of the card as originally retrieved (01–12). Part of the original snapshot used to detect concurrent changes before saving.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY
variables.description: The two-digit expiry day of the card as originally retrieved. Part of the original snapshot used to detect concurrent changes before saving.

variables.name: CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD
variables.description: The card's active/inactive status (Y or N) as originally retrieved from the database. Part of the original snapshot used to detect if another user has changed the card status before the update is committed.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-DETAILS
variables.description: Holds the updated card data as entered by the bank staff member on the update screen. These values are validated and then held for staff confirmation before being written to the card database.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-ACCTID
variables.description: The account ID as entered or confirmed by the staff member on the update screen. Must be 11 digits and non-zero; used to identify which account's card is being updated.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-CARDID
variables.description: The 16-digit card number as entered or confirmed by the staff member. Identifies the specific card record to be updated in the card database.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD
variables.description: The card's CVV security code carried forward into the new details structure. Not editable by staff on this screen; preserved to ensure the full card record can be reconstructed when writing the update.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA
variables.description: Groups the editable card data fields as entered by the staff member. These are the values that will replace the existing card record in the database after validation and confirmation.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-CRDNAME
variables.description: The updated embossed cardholder name entered by the staff member. Must contain only alphabetic characters and spaces. This is the name that will appear on the card record after the update is saved.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-EXPIRAION-DATE
variables.description: The updated card expiry date entered by the staff member, broken into year, month, and day components. Each component is individually validated before the update is allowed to proceed.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-EXPYEAR
variables.description: The updated four-digit expiry year entered by the staff member (must be between 1950 and 2099). Determines when the card will expire and is written to the card record upon confirmed update.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-EXPMON
variables.description: The updated two-digit expiry month entered by the staff member (must be 01–12). Together with the expiry year, defines the card's validity period.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY
variables.description: The updated two-digit expiry day entered by the staff member. Completes the expiry date stored on the card record.

variables.name: CCUP-NEW-CRDSTCD
variables.description: The updated card active/inactive status entered by the staff member (Y = active, N = inactive). Controls whether the card can be used for transactions. Must be exactly Y or N; any other value is rejected.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-RECORD
variables.description: The complete card record structure that will be physically written to the card database file (CARDDAT) when the staff member confirms the update. Assembled from the validated new details and written as a single record to replace the existing card entry.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-NUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number that serves as the primary key of the record being written to the card database. Identifies exactly which card record is being updated.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The 11-digit account ID stored in the card record being written. Links the card to its parent account in the database.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-CVV-CD
variables.description: The three-digit CVV security code stored in the card record being written. Not modified by this update screen; carried forward unchanged from the original record to preserve the card's security credentials.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-EMBOSSED-NAME
variables.description: The cardholder's name as it will be stored in the updated card record. This is the validated new name entered by the staff member, which physically represents the name embossed on the card.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-EXPIRAION-DATE
variables.description: The card's expiry date as it will be stored in the updated card record (formatted as a 10-character string, e.g. YYYY/MM/DD). Represents the date after which the card is no longer valid for use.

variables.name: CARD-UPDATE-ACTIVE-STATUS
variables.description: The card's active or inactive status as it will be stored in the updated card record (Y = active, N = inactive). Determines whether the card is currently usable for transactions after the update is saved.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved padding space within the card update record structure. Ensures the record written to the card database file meets the required fixed-length record size, accommodating any additional fields that may exist in the physical file layout.

variables.name: WS-COMMAREA
variables.description: A 2000-byte general-purpose communication area used to pass data between this program and other CardDemo programs (such as the main menu or card list screen) via CICS COMMAREA. Carries context such as user identity, account information, and navigation state across program transfers.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area passed into this program when it is invoked. Contains data sent from the previously executing program (e.g. the card list screen), such as the selected card number and account ID, enabling the update program to know which card to work with.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A minimal placeholder within DFHCOMMAREA. Satisfies the COBOL requirement that a group item must have at least one subordinate field; the actual COMMAREA content is accessed via WS-COMMAREA which overlays or is populated from this area.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.description: This is the main orchestration paragraph that controls the entire credit card update workflow. It determines the user's current stage in the update process and routes them to the appropriate next step — whether that is displaying the update screen, validating changes, confirming an update, or exiting to another screen.

paragraphs.name: COMMON-RETURN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the controlled exit from the card update screen, packaging any pending status or error messages together with the full application session state before returning control to the CICS transaction manager, ready for the next user interaction on the same screen.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the main processing routine, returning control cleanly after all credit card update workflow steps have been completed or aborted.

paragraphs.name: 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the intake and validation of all data entered by bank staff on the card update screen, then ensures the application is configured to redisplay the same screen — retaining any error messages — so staff can review and correct their input before proceeding.

paragraphs.name: 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the input processing routine, allowing the workflow to cleanly return control after all user inputs have been evaluated and handled.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the card update details entered by bank staff on the screen and loads them into a working copy of the new card data, ready for validation. Empty or placeholder fields (asterisks or blanks) are treated as absent/cleared values, ensuring only genuine staff input is carried forward into the update workflow.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the designated exit point for the screen data reception routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control after capturing staff input from the card update screen.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the validation of all data entered by bank staff on the card update screen. It determines whether to validate search keys for initial card retrieval, or to validate the editable card detail fields (cardholder name, active status, expiry month and year) when changes have been submitted for an existing retrieved card record.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the input validation routine, marking the end of all card detail checks (name, expiry date, and active status) before the workflow proceeds to the next stage.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the account number entered by bank staff before a card record can be retrieved. It ensures the account number is present, numeric, and exactly 11 digits, rejecting the lookup and prompting correction if any rule is violated.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account field validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after all account-related input checks have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1220-EDIT-CARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the card number entered by bank staff, ensuring it is present, fully numeric, and exactly 16 digits before allowing the card record retrieval to proceed. Any violation is flagged with an appropriate error message and the workflow is halted at this step.

paragraphs.name: 1220-EDIT-CARD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card data validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after all card field validations have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-NAME
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the embossed cardholder name entered by bank staff, ensuring it is neither blank nor contains any non-alphabetic characters (such as numbers or special symbols). Only names consisting entirely of letters and spaces are accepted, enforcing the bank's data quality rules for what is physically printed on the card.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-NAME-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the cardholder name validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after name validation has completed.

paragraphs.name: 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that the card active status entered by bank staff is acceptable for processing. It ensures the status field is neither blank nor an invalid value — only 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive) are permitted, in line with the bank's card management rules.

paragraphs.name: 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card active status validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after the status check (Y/N) has been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the card expiry month entered by bank staff, ensuring it is present and represents a real calendar month (1–12) before the update can proceed. Any invalid or missing value is flagged as an input error and an appropriate message is prepared for display.

paragraphs.name: 1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card expiry month validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after the expiry month check has been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the card expiry year entered by bank staff, ensuring it is present and falls within the accepted calendar range (1950–2099) before the update can proceed. Any invalid or missing expiry year is flagged as an input error and an appropriate message is prepared for display.

paragraphs.name: 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card expiry year validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after expiry year validation has been completed.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION
paragraphs.description: This paragraph acts as the central workflow controller for the card update process, routing each user interaction to the correct next step based on the current stage of the update workflow and the action the staff member has taken. It determines whether to fetch card details, validate changes, request confirmation, commit the update, or handle errors — ensuring the correct business process step is executed at each point in the update journey.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the workflow routing logic that determines which stage of the card update process to execute. It marks the end of the action-decision routine, returning control to the main processing flow.

paragraphs.name: 3000-SEND-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full preparation and delivery of the card update screen to the bank staff member's terminal. It coordinates screen initialisation, data population, informational messaging, field attribute configuration, and final screen transmission as a single end-to-end display operation.

paragraphs.name: 3000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the designated exit point for the screen-sending routine, providing a clean termination anchor that other parts of the update workflow jump to after completing all screen preparation and display logic.

paragraphs.name: 3100-SCREEN-INIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initialises the Credit Card Update screen by clearing any residual data and populating the screen header with standard identifying information — application titles, transaction identity, program name, and the current date and time — so that staff see a clean, correctly labelled screen before any card data is displayed.

paragraphs.name: 3100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen initialisation routine, marking the end of the screen setup process with no additional business logic of its own. It acts as a structural boundary that allows the program to cleanly return control after the screen has been prepared for display to bank staff.

paragraphs.name: 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the credit card update screen by populating the display fields with the appropriate card data depending on where the staff member is in the update workflow. It ensures the screen always reflects the correct state — whether showing a blank form, the original retrieved card details, or the staff member's pending changes.

paragraphs.name: 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen variable setup routine, marking the end of the process that prepares card detail fields for display to bank staff. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator for the setup workflow step.

paragraphs.name: 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG
paragraphs.description: This paragraph determines the appropriate guidance or status message to display to bank staff based on the current stage of the card update workflow, then places that message and any error notification onto the screen for the staff member to read.

paragraphs.name: 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the informational message setup routine, marking the end of the process that prepares status and guidance messages for display to bank staff. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator for the message preparation workflow.

paragraphs.name: 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph configures the visual presentation of the card update screen by setting which fields are editable or read-only, positioning the cursor on the most relevant field, and applying colour-coding to highlight errors or required actions — all based on the current stage of the update workflow and the outcome of field-level validations.

paragraphs.name: 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen attribute setup routine, marking the end of the process that configures how fields are displayed to bank staff on the card update screen. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator for the paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 3400-SEND-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the credit card update screen to the bank staff member's terminal, displaying the current state of the workflow (card details, validation messages, or confirmation prompts) and positioning the cursor ready for input. It clears any previous screen content and unlocks the keyboard so staff can interact with the updated display.

paragraphs.name: 3400-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that displays the credit card update screen to bank staff. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural terminator for the screen display workflow step.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the current credit card record from the database using the account number and card number provided by the bank staff, then captures a snapshot of the card's existing details to serve as a baseline for detecting any concurrent modifications before an update is committed.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-DATA-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the designated exit point for the card data retrieval routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after a card record lookup has been attempted, whether successful or not.

paragraphs.name: 9100-GETCARD-BYACCTCARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves a specific credit card record from the card database using the card number entered by bank staff. It validates whether the card exists and handles errors appropriately, ensuring staff are informed if the account/card combination cannot be found or if a system error occurs.

paragraphs.name: 9100-GETCARD-BYACCTCARD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card retrieval routine, marking the end of the process that looks up a credit card record by account number and card number. It provides a structured return path so that control is cleanly handed back to the calling workflow step after the card lookup has completed.

paragraphs.name: 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs the final committed write of updated credit card details to the database, enforcing record locking and concurrent-modification checks before saving. It ensures that only one user can update a card at a time and that no other user has altered the record since it was first retrieved for editing.

paragraphs.name: 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card update write processing routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling workflow step after all update operations have been attempted.

paragraphs.name: 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC
paragraphs.description: This paragraph acts as a concurrent-modification guard: it compares the card record currently held in the database against the snapshot captured when staff first retrieved it, to detect whether another user has altered the card in the interim. If a discrepancy is found, the update is blocked, the stored snapshot is refreshed with the latest database values, and staff are redirected to re-review the current state of the card before attempting to save again.

paragraphs.name: 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the concurrent-modification check routine, marking the end of the process that verifies whether another user has altered the card record since it was first retrieved. It also incorporates shared logic for capturing which function key the bank staff member pressed, enabling correct navigation and workflow decisions.

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable system failures during the card update process. It ensures that when a fatal error occurs, staff are informed, the failure is attributed to this program, and the transaction is forcibly terminated with a recognisable error code to allow operations teams to investigate.

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the abnormal termination handling routine, marking the boundary where abend error processing ends and control flow concludes. It ensures the program terminates cleanly after any critical failure has been handled.
